subject: Post-demo: AegisMetrics networking & SDK integration playbook
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Ravi Shah <ravi@aegismetrics.com>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@aegismetrics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-11T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: AegisMetrics networking & SDK integration playbook

Hi Ravi / Elena —

Great to meet you both on the demo today. Thanks for walking through the ingestion and reranking use case; there was a lot of alignment. I promised a concise follow-up on architecture and next steps focused on the networking and SDK integration bits.

Key notes from today: 
- Primary integration: server-side API calls from Aegis back end to Redwood API using SDK (preferred).
- Private connectivity ask: you want a predictable egress IP and mutual TLS option for high-sensitivity payloads.
- Routing/structured output: you’ll use the tool-calling path for enrichment; embeddings + reranker to power similarity scoring.

Immediate asks we heard from your infra team:
1) VPC endpoint or dedicated egress IPs (IP allowlist)
2) DNS resolution for private endpoint and TLS verification
3) SDK auth pattern (short-lived keys / mTLS certs) and token rotation
4) Expected throughput (concurrent reqs / max tokens) for sizing dedicated capacity

Attached is an initial "Aegis networking & SDK playbook" (aegis_playbook_v1.pdf) and a simplified network diagram (network-diagram.png). High-level next steps I propose:
- Ben to scope the VPC endpoint vs. NAT egress options and share tradeoffs (security, latency, cost).
- Priyom to draft the SDK auth flows (mTLS + short-lived token option) and sample code.
- Schedule a 60-min tech deep-dive next week with your infra and engineering leads to finalize the Mutual Action Plan.

Can you confirm availability for a deep-dive on Aug 14th 9:00–10:00 PT or Aug 15th 11:00–12:00 PT? Also, any constraints around egress IP ranges we should know about?

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: aegis_playbook_v1.pdf, network-diagram.png

From: Ravi Shah <ravi@aegismetrics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@aegismetrics.com>
Date: 2028-08-11T18:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: AegisMetrics networking & SDK integration playbook

Thanks Hannah — appreciate the clear recap and materials. Quick answers from our side: 
- Deep-dive: Aug 14th 9:00–10:00 PT works for our infra + platform engineers.
- Egress constraints: we run in a VPC in AWS (us-west-2). We can accept a small set of allowed IPs (preferably a /28 or equivalent) or a private endpoint if Redwood can support a VPC endpoint in our account.
- mTLS: we prefer mutual TLS for the highest-sensitivity calls (PII tagging), but short-lived tokens for lower-sensitivity interactions would be ideal.

Two questions before the deep-dive:
1) For the routing fallback, can Redwood route to a lower-cost model variant automatically if dedicated capacity is saturated?
2) How does the SDK expose structured output and tool-calling (we want JSON-first responses scoped to a schema)?

We'll review the playbook and come prepared with our network/SEC diagram.

—Ravi
Ravi Shah
Head of Platform, AegisMetrics
ravi@aegismetrics.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Ravi Shah <ravi@aegismetrics.com>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@aegismetrics.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-12T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: AegisMetrics networking & SDK integration playbook

Ravi —

Good questions. Short answers up front, details below and attached: network-diagram.png (annotated) and mutual_action_plan.docx (MMP draft).

1) VPC endpoint vs. egress IPs:
- We support two primary private connectivity patterns:
  a) VPC onramp (private endpoint) — we can provision a PrivateLink / VPC endpoint in your VPC so traffic stays within the cloud fabric; ideal for strict egress policies and minimizes public exposure. Requires peering/config within your account and an initial network handshake.
  b) Fixed egress IPs — we can reserve a small pool of IPs for your tenant (recommended if you cannot accept a private endpoint). Works well with IP allowlist setups.
Tradeoffs: endpoint = lower blast radius and simpler DNS/TLS; fixed IP = faster to stand up if you cannot accept connections into your VPC.

2) Routing/fallbacks:
- Our smart routing will surface model variants by policy (latency/cost). You can configure a fallback chain: dedicated -> hosted-high-throughput -> hosted-cost-optimized. We can enforce SLOs and circuit-breaker thresholds so fallbacks are explicit and logged.

3) SDK structured output / tool-calling:
- SDK supports a structured-response API where you declare a JSON schema and the model returns JSON conformant output. Tool-calling is implemented via a staged invocation where the model returns tool intents and the SDK orchestrates tool execution (post-hook). We'll bring sample code and a small sandbox during the deep-dive.

Action items before Aug 14th deep-dive:
- Priyom: attach sample mTLS cert rotation flow & short-lived token example.
- Hannah: set up the calendar invite and include infra contacts.
- Ravi: if you choose endpoint option, please share the VPC ID and a preferred subnet range for the endpoint. If fixed IP, share your IP allowlist rule template.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
+1 (650) 555-0123

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.docx, network-diagram.png

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Ravi Shah <ravi@aegismetrics.com>, Elena Morales <elena.morales@aegismetrics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-14T10:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: AegisMetrics networking & SDK integration playbook

Ravi / Elena —

Thanks for confirming the time — looking forward to the deep-dive in 30 minutes. In advance of the call I pushed two snippets into the Drive folder:
- mTLS-cert-rotation.md (example rotation flow + verification checks)
- sdk-auth-samples.zip (short examples for Node/Python showing token renewal + header patterns)

Quick technical clarifications we’ll cover during the deep-dive:
- Certificate trust: we support customer-provided certs pinned to the tenant and CA-managed certs for short-lived mTLS where Redwood rotates certs and provides a rotation webhook.
- DNS: if using PrivateLink, we will instruct you to create a private hosted zone that resolves the endpoint hostname to the endpoint interface(s); we also support split-horizon DNS for hybrid setups.
- Embeddings/reranker: recommend batching embeddings client-side at ~1–2k items per request and using the dedicated reranker endpoint for the top-K sort to keep latency predictable.

See you on the call — attaching the Drive links here for convenience: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abcDEF_g3

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Principal Integration Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai
